nodes.name: Electrodeposition of NiFe (10 g/L FeCl2)
nodes.procedure: Cu sheets (4 cm × 1 cm) were mechanically polished with up to grade 3000 sandpapers, then ultrasonically degreased with acetone for 15 min. Before electrodeposition and to properly activate the surface, 20% HCl was used. The electrodeposition bath contained NiCl2·6H2O (1M), CaCl2·2H2O (1.2M), and FeCl2·4H2O (10 g L^-1). The temperature was fixed at 60 °C, and the pH of the solution was measured to be about 2.5. A Ni sheet was used as the anode, and a steady current density of -40 mA cm^-2 was applied for 10 min. After the coating process, the samples were washed with distilled water and then left to dry at room temperature.

nodes.characterization_summary: FE-SEM reveals urchin-like morphology with numerous micro/nano-scale cones for NieFe samples at Fe2+ concentrations of 20-50 g L-1.
nodes.evidence_snippet: by the increase of Fe2+ content, urchin-like morphology appears. As schematically shown in Fig. 1f, by increasing Fe2+ in the electrodeposition bath, many sharp nanocones grow on the sphere-like structures, which form the urchin-like structure.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS analysis of all NieFe samples shows increasing Fe content from 14.31 wt% (10 g L-1) to 31.78 wt% (50 g L-1) with Ni:Fe ratios of 85.69:14.31, 75.74:24.26, 71.28:28.32, 69.74:30.26, and 68.22:31.78 respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD of optimal NieFe sample (30 g L-1 Fe2+) shows Ni (111) and Ni (200) peaks indicating FCC crystalline structure with no detectable Fe peaks, suggesting Ni-Fe solid solution.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ni (111) and Ni (200) peaks indicate the FCC crystalline structure. It is noteworthy that no Fe peaks can be detected in the spectrum. This means that Ni and Fe atoms may have formed a solid solution regarding their close atomic radius.
